name: Prayer (Means of Grace)

objectives.text: Identify prayer as speaking to God our Father in heaven
Recite the Lord's Prayer and name it as the prayer Jesus taught his disciples
Identify Bible passages that teach God hears the prayers of his people
Describe times in the Gospels when Jesus prayed and what he prayed about
Give an example of each part of prayer: adoration, confession, thanksgiving, and supplication
Explain why Christians pray in the name of Jesus
Explain the meaning of the preface and each of the six petitions of the Lord's Prayer
Compare private prayer with family and corporate prayer using examples from Scripture
Explain why the Reformed tradition names prayer, with the Word and sacraments, as an ordinary means of grace
Compose a prayer of intercession for others, including those who oppose or mistreat them, following Jesus' command
Analyze the requests Paul makes in his prayers for the churches and what they show about his priorities
Analyze psalms of lament and confession as models for bringing sorrow and sin to God in prayer
Interpret the role of the Holy Spirit and of Christ in interceding for believers
Explain how the Reformed tradition teaches that God ordains prayer as a means through which he accomplishes his purposes
Explain the biblical practice of fasting and its relationship to prayer
Analyze the conditions Scripture gives for acceptable prayer, such as asking in faith, according to God's will, and with confession of sin
Explain how Scripture accounts for prayers that God answers differently than requested
Construct an account of the believer's access to God in prayer grounded in Christ's high priesthood and the priesthood of believers
Compare the Reformed teaching that prayer is directed to God alone through Christ alone with the practice of praying to saints or angels
Evaluate the difference between mystical contemplation and biblical meditation on God's Word
Evaluate deistic and fatalistic objections to petitionary prayer using the Reformed doctrine of providence
Design a plan for regular personal and family prayer structured by the petitions of the Lord's Prayer and the parts of prayer

changes: Kept and reworded real competencies: prayer as speaking to God, the Lord's Prayer, God hearing prayer, Jesus' prayer life, the parts of prayer, praying in Jesus' name, private versus corporate prayer, praying for enemies (now composing an intercessory prayer), Paul's prayers, the Spirit's intercession (now with Christ's), fasting, and priesthood of believers. Reframed 'God always hears us' as identifying passages so it is a knowledge objective. Merged the overlapping sovereignty, providence, and anti-deism objectives into a grade 9 explanation of prayer as an ordained means and a grade 12 evaluation of deistic and fatalistic objections. Added missing competencies: explaining the six petitions, prayer as an ordinary means of grace, psalms of lament and confession as models, conditions of acceptable prayer, unanswered prayer, prayer to God alone versus to saints, and designing a personal and family prayer plan. Replaced chapter-level references with verse ranges and anchored confessions to WSC Q88 and Q98-107, WCF 5 and 21, and Heidelberg Q116-119.
